controls.desc: The committee shall ensure that technology procurements are aligned with the IT strategy approved by the board.

controls.desc: The management shall formulate an appropriate MIS to monitor the implementation of the IT governance and risk management framework, as part of management-approved procedures.

controls.desc: Board and senior management-level engagement along with a clear chain of accountability is critical to the success of FI cyber security action plan.

controls.desc: Quality assurance standards shall address issues such as validation of project assumptions, adherence to project standards and testing of a product's performance.

controls.desc: FIs shall form an appropriate forum/structure to monitor the process of technology-related procurements.

controls.desc: FIs shall formulate procedures on system development and all related documentation including development, testing, trainings, production, operational administration and user manuals.

controls.desc: FIs shall define roles and responsibilities of officers to ensure that all changes to system, application and configuration documentation are made according to prescribed standards.

controls.desc: For critical projects/systems, FIs shall conduct a post-implementation review at the end of a project to validate the application's operational performance.

controls.desc: FIs shall assess the relative success of the project by comparing planned and actual cost, benefits and completion time.

controls.title: Record reasons when planned objectives do not materialize
controls.desc: FIs shall record reasons in a post-implementation evaluation report if the planned objectives do not materialize.

controls.title: Present post-implementation report to senior management

controls.desc: Management shall establish a clear information security policy aligned with organizational objectives, approved by senior levels, and reviewed periodically.

controls.title: Information Security Risk Assessment
controls.desc: Risk assessments shall include quantifying risks, determining management priorities, and periodically updating results.

controls.title: Information Security Risk Treatment
controls.desc: Risk treatment decisions shall be made following risk assessments.

controls.title: Information Security Coordination
controls.desc: Coordination shall be undertaken by authorized representatives with required technical skills.

controls.desc: Responsibilities shall be clearly defined and include non-disclosure agreements.

controls.desc: Validate the operational effectiveness of security controls through penetration testing.

controls.title: Scenario-based Risk Assessment
controls.desc: Perform regular risk assessments considering SWIFT-specific cyber threat scenarios.

controls.title: Secure Backup and Recovery
controls.desc: Maintain secure backups of SWIFT-related systems and data for recovery purposes.

controls.desc: Implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations.

controls.desc: Conflicting duties and conflicting areas of responsibility shall be segregated to reduce opportunities for unauthorized or unintentional modification or misuse of the organization's assets.

controls.desc: Management shall require all personnel to apply information security in accordance with the established information security policy and topic-specific policies and procedures of the organization.

controls.title: Contact with Authorities
controls.desc: The organization shall establish and maintain contact with relevant authorities such as law enforcement, regulatory bodies, and supervisory authorities.

controls.title: Contact with Special Interest Groups
controls.desc: The organization shall establish and maintain contact with special interest groups or other specialist security forums and professional associations.

controls.desc: Information security shall be integrated into project management regardless of the type of the project.

controls.title: COSO Principle 2: Board Independence and Oversight
controls.desc: The board of directors demonstrates independence from management and exercises oversight of the development and performance of internal control.

controls.title: COSO Principle 3: Management Establishes Structure, Authority, and Responsibility
controls.desc: Management establishes, with board oversight, structures, reporting lines, and appropriate authorities and responsibilities in the pursuit of objectives.

controls.title: COSO Principle 5: Accountability for Internal Control
controls.desc: The entity holds individuals accountable for their internal control responsibilities in the pursuit of objectives.

controls.title: COSO Principle 13: Quality Information for Internal Control
controls.desc: The entity obtains or generates and uses relevant, quality information to support the functioning of internal control.

controls.title: COSO Principle 14: Internal Communication
controls.desc: The entity internally communicates information, including objectives and responsibilities for internal control, necessary to support the functioning of internal control.

controls.title: COSO Principle 15: External Communication
controls.desc: The entity communicates with external parties regarding matters affecting the functioning of internal control.

controls.desc: The entity selects and develops control activities that contribute to the mitigation of risks to the achievement of objectives to acceptable levels.

controls.title: COSO Principle 11: Selects and Develops General Controls over Technology
controls.desc: The entity also selects and develops general control activities over technology to support the achievement of objectives.

controls.desc: The entity deploys control activities through policies that establish what is expected and in procedures that put policies into action.
